text:
Someone else pushed commits to `main` after you last fetched, so your local `main` isn't a descendant of the remote's — Git refuses the push rather than discarding their work.

To fix:

```
git fetch origin
git log --oneline HEAD..origin/main   # see what they added
git rebase origin/main                # or: git merge origin/main
git push
```

Pick rebase if your commits aren't shared yet (linear history, cleaner); pick merge if you've already pushed this branch elsewhere or others have it. If the rebase hits conflicts, resolve, `git add`, `git rebase --continue`.

Don't reach for `git push --force` here — it would delete the remote commits you don't have. `--force-with-lease` is the safe variant, but it's only appropriate if you *intend* to drop those commits, which isn't the case for a shared `main`.
